subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-chunk deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should the permanent block-streaming contract preserve overflow paragraph boundaries with explicit seam metadata, reserve separator width in the size split, or intentionally accept a partial text-only repair?
rationale: The code path and bug are clear, but the near-maxChars case cannot be solved by simply appending text without either changing split behavior or carrying boundary semantics outside the text payload.

options.title: Require a complete shared fix
options.body: Choose one candidate or replacement implementation that preserves paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-maxChars splits before merge.

options.title: Adopt explicit seam metadata
options.body: Ask the branch to carry paragraph/newline/hard-split boundary metadata through chunker, subscriber, and coalescer if text-only chunks cannot satisfy both reconstruction and maxChars constraints.

options.title: Accept partial text-only behavior
options.body: Maintainers may knowingly land the common-case improvement while leaving the exact overflow boundary documented on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Require a complete shared fix
recommendation.body: Choose one candidate or replacement implementation that preserves paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-maxChars splits before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent ownership signal across the affected chunking/coalescing surfaces and is the best available owner for the boundary-contract choice.
